0-northborough-road-common-driveway.name: 0 Northborough Road common driveway special permit
0-northborough-road-common-driveway.description: Special permit application to allow 15 feet of frontage on an 8-acre parcel to divide the land into two residential building lots served by a common driveway.
0-northborough-road-common-driveway.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a frontage variance on September 16, 2026, allowing a 15-foot Massachusetts Water Resources Authority easement to serve as frontage for two proposed residential lots on a common driveway. At the same meeting, the board accepted the applicant's withdrawal of its companion special permit application. The project must now seek subdivision approval from the Planning Board, as town counsel advised that an Approval Not Required plan cannot rely on a variance.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 16 to approve the frontage variance and accepted the withdrawal of the special permit.
A relative of the applicant spoke in favor of granting the variance, citing past town precedent for access through a water department right-of-way.

0-southville-road.name: 0 Southville Road apartment development
0-southville-road.description: Proposed construction of two apartment buildings and associated infrastructure at 0 Southville Road.
0-southville-road.status: The proposed 60-unit apartment development at 0 Southville Road remains under environmental review, with its Notice of Intent and stormwater management permit hearings continued by the Conservation Commission on October 8, 2026. The two-building project falls within the MBTA Communities zoning district, requiring at least six affordable units. The Affordable Housing Trust has also explored whether municipal subsidies could buy down additional affordable units, awaiting cost estimates from the developer.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on October 8, 2026, to continue the Notice of Intent and stormwater permit hearings while awaiting revised plans responding to peer review.

positions.body: Board of Trustees of the Affordable Housing Trust
positions.detail: Reviewed the 60-unit concept in March 2026 and requested cost projections from the developer to see if town funds could subsidize units beyond the 10 percent required.

0-valley-road-trail.name: 0 Valley Road footbridge and trail
0-valley-road-trail.description: Proposed construction of a wooden boardwalk and trail connection on Southborough Open Land Foundation land off Valley Road.
0-valley-road-trail.status: The Conservation Commission approved an Order of Conditions on July 29, 2026, allowing an Eagle Scout project to construct a wooden boardwalk and dirt trail on Southborough Open Land Foundation land at 0 Valley Road. Abutters opposed the application, raising concerns over traffic, parking along a narrow road, trespassing, and wetland disruption. With the public hearing closed and environmental conditions established, the project is cleared to proceed following the standard appeal window.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0-1 on July 29 to issue an Order of Conditions with standard and special conditions after confirming modern treated lumber poses no water toxicity risk.
Spoke in favor of the project on June 25, stating that the proposed boardwalk and trail support its mission to offer passive recreation.
Valley Road abutters opposed the trail, citing safety and congestion from parking on a narrow road, loss of privacy, trespassing into yards, and disturbance to wildlife.

1-overlook-drive-pool.name: 1 Overlook Drive swimming pool
1-overlook-drive-pool.description: Notice of Intent to construct an inground swimming pool, patio, and cabana within the wetland buffer zone at 1 Overlook Drive.
1-overlook-drive-pool.status: The project is approved. On October 8, 2026, the Conservation Commission voted 4-0 to close the hearing and issue an Order of Conditions for the pool, patio, and cabana. Approval is subject to special conditions requiring eight native shrubs to be maintained in perpetuity and a pre-construction site visit to review machinery access protections.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on October 8, 2026, to approve the Order of Conditions with requirements for native plantings and pre-construction access review.

104-boston-road-water-appeal.name: 104 Boston Road water bill appeal
104-boston-road-water-appeal.description: Abatement appeal before the Water Commissioners regarding an underground leak and high water bill at 104 Boston Road.
104-boston-road-water-appeal.status: The appeal has been resolved. On September 15, the Select Board, acting as Water Commissioners, voted 4-0-1 to grant a partial abatement on the leak-related water bill, lowering the charge from $2,872.03 to $1,100. No further review or action is scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0-1 on Sep 15 to grant a partial abatement, setting the final bill amount at $1,100.
A resident urged full bill relief for the property and called on the town to expedite smart water meter installations to prevent leak surprises.

12-darlene-drive-variance.name: 12 Darlene Drive setback variance
12-darlene-drive-variance.description: Front setback variance request to construct a covered front porch addition encroaching 1.5 feet into the setback at 12 Darlene Drive.
12-darlene-drive-variance.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously approved the front setback variance in March 2026, allowing a covered front porch addition to encroach 1.5 feet into the 30-foot setback. The board determined the request was modest and justified by unique site conditions caused by an oil pipeline easement. The statutory filing and appeal periods have since elapsed.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on March 18, 2026, to grant the variance, citing site constraints from an oil pipeline easement and the modest scale of the encroachment.
Neighbors submitted letters supporting the variance request.

12-wood-street-special-permit.name: 12 Wood Street special permit
12-wood-street-special-permit.description: Special permit application to alter a pre-existing non-conforming single-family residential structure with a rear deck at 12 Wood Street.
12-wood-street-special-permit.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously approved the special permit to alter a pre-existing non-conforming single-family structure at 12 Wood Street. The permit addresses an as-built survey finding that a newly built rear deck sits 13 feet from the rear lot line bordering the Sudbury River rather than the planned 16 feet. With no objections raised by the board or the public, the board's review is complete.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on April 15, 2026, to approve the special permit application as written.

14-newton-street.name: 14 Newton Street garage and ADU
14-newton-street.description: Notice of Intent to construct a detached garage with an accessory dwelling unit and replacement septic in the wetland buffer at 14 Newton Street.
14-newton-street.status: The proposed garage, accessory dwelling unit, and replacement septic system at 14 Newton Street have secured key local approvals. The Conservation Commission approved an Order of Conditions in July 2026, and the Board of Health granted required setback variances in August 2026 despite concerns about expanding flow on a constrained lot. Before starting construction, the applicant must install erosion controls and obtain an inspection.

positions.detail: Voted 2-1 on Aug 11 to grant septic setback reductions from a town drain line, despite the chair dissenting against granting variance relief to expand system capacity on a constrained lot.
Voted 3-0-1 on Jul 29 to issue an Order of Conditions following plan adjustments to an infiltration drywell for roof runoff.

154-turnpike-road.name: 154 Turnpike Road site plan modification
154-turnpike-road.description: Major site plan approval modification and landscaping compliance for commercial development at 154 Turnpike Road.
154-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board approved the major site plan modification for the Chase Bank location on October 19, 2026, resolving earlier non-compliance issues regarding lighting and landscaping. The approval includes conditions governing timer and dimmer controls for exterior light fixtures, landscape maintenance, accessible parking space layout, and as-built plan submissions. Capital Group Properties must now submit revised plans with Planning Board endorsement blocks and final as-builts to conclude the process.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Oct 19, 2026 to approve the site plan modification decision with conditions covering lighting, landscaping, and parking.

170-woodland-road-coc.name: 170 Woodland Road Certificate of Compliance
170-woodland-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review for pool, patio, and drainage work within wetland resource areas at 170 Woodland Road.
170-woodland-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission approved the Certificate of Compliance for 170 Woodland Road on June 4, 2026, closing out the project's wetland permit. The conservation agent confirmed that required mitigation trees and plantings were inspected and found in healthy condition. The matter is resolved and no further action is pending.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on June 4, 2026, to issue the Certificate of Compliance after inspecting the site's mitigation plantings.

200-turnpike-road.name: 200 Turnpike Road site plan compliance
200-turnpike-road.description: Site plan compliance, occupancy permitting, and landscape performance bonding for a commercial facility at 200 Turnpike Road.
200-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board accepted a $30,000 surety agreement and voted 5-0 to recommend that the building inspector issue a full certificate of occupancy for the commercial facility at 200 Turnpike Road. The recommendation followed agreement on resolving winter landscaping die-off and slope erosion, backed by a performance bond through October 2027. A follow-up inspection is scheduled for fall 2027 to ensure plant survival and slope stability.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22 to accept a $30,000 surety agreement and recommend a full certificate of occupancy subject to landscaping conditions.

200-turnpike-road.next: Follow-up inspection for landscaping and slope stability by October 1, 2027

2027-masstrails-grant.name: 2027 MassTrails grant application
2027-masstrails-grant.description: Application and regional school partnerships for up to $100,000 in state MassTrails grant funding for trail improvements.
2027-masstrails-grant.status: The Trails Committee is drafting an application for up to $100,000 in FY27 MassTrails grant funding for trail improvements, including a Peninsula Trail bridge. The committee is coordinating educational partnerships with local schools and securing letters of support ahead of the state deadline in early February 2027. The Recreation Commission voted unanimously on November 12 to endorse the project, and additional working sessions will continue through December.

positions.detail: Actively preparing the grant application and conducting outreach to local school districts and municipal boards for support.
Voted 4-0 on Nov 12, 2026, to write a letter of support for the Peninsula Trail bridge application.

2027-masstrails-grant.next: Trails Committee grant planning meeting the week of November 18, 2026.

2030-master-plan-update.name: 2030 Master Plan update
2030-master-plan-update.description: Strategy, funding, and consultant selection for updating Southborough's comprehensive Master Plan for 2030.
2030-master-plan-update.status: The town is in the early planning stages for its 2030 Master Plan update, with the Master Plan Implementation Committee proposing a hybrid model that pairs volunteer committees with a light-touch consultant. The committee recommended establishing a 15-member subcommittee in 2027 to pursue technical assistance grants ahead of an FY28 or FY29 funding request. Planning Board members cautioned that municipal budget pressures and a potential Proposition 2 1/2 override could make Town Meeting appropriations difficult, urging reliance on state grants. The Planning Board took no formal action and plans to place the strategy on a future agenda.

positions.detail: Recommends creating a subcommittee in 2027 and engaging a consultant to guide volunteers on focused priority themes, funded by grants or a town appropriation.
Heard presentation on Oct 19 without taking action, with members emphasizing the need for state grants due to municipal budget constraints and a potential tax override.

21-coslin-drive-costco.name: 21 Coslin Drive Costco development
21-coslin-drive-costco.description: Site plan and special permit review for a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco retail warehouse and 30-position gas station at 21 Coslin Drive.
21-coslin-drive-costco.status: The proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position gas station is under major site plan and special permit review before the Planning Board, with the statutory decision deadline extended to December 18, 2026. While the Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously granted variance relief for retaining walls and lighting in July 2026, the Planning Board and neighbors are scrutinizing severe traffic impacts, intersection failures, and residential cut-through truck traffic. The board is evaluating peer review findings and proposed developer mitigation, including road repaving, signal timing adjustments, and travel demand programs. The public hearing resumes on November 16, 2026.

positions.detail: Reviewing site plans and special permits while raising sharp questions about intersection delays, U-turn volumes on Route 9, and the lack of enforceable off-site truck routing restrictions.
Voted 4-0 on July 15, 2026, to approve variances for retaining walls up to 31 feet and light poles up to 36.5 feet.

Residents and business owners voiced strong objections over regional gridlock, school bus delays, existing level-of-service F intersections, and heavy truck traffic cutting through residential roads like Parkerville, Flagg, and Southville.

21-coslin-drive-costco.next: Continued public hearing before the Planning Board on November 16, 2026

21-highland-street-use.name: 21 Highland Street future use
21-highland-street-use.description: Planning for municipal department space allocation, community use, or potential sale of the town-owned building at 21 Highland Street.
21-highland-street-use.status: Space planning for 21 Highland Street remains under review as Youth and Family Services prepares to move to the Flagg School in late October. The Recreation Commission plans to absorb the vacated office space to expand after-school STEM and arts programming and create a civic meeting room. However, the long-term future of the municipal facility remains open following Select Board discussions regarding a potential sale of the property.

positions.detail: Supports repurposing space vacated by Youth and Family Services for after-school programming and town committee meeting rooms.

21-southville-road-coc.name: 21 Southville Road Certificate of Compliance
21-southville-road-coc.description: Request for a Certificate of Compliance under DEP file 290-1142 for a sunroom and patio within the wetland buffer zone at 21 Southville Road.
21-southville-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 on October 8 to issue a Certificate of Compliance for 21 Southville Road. The decision closes out the permit for converting a porch into a sunroom and patio within the wetland buffer zone. The conservation agent verified that the work is finished, the site's soils are stable, and a natural fence buffer was preserved.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Oct 8 to approve the Certificate of Compliance after confirming the work is complete and the site is stable.

22-newton-street-variance.name: 22 Newton Street garage variance
22-newton-street-variance.description: Variance petition under Section 174-8.3(D)(3)(b) to construct a detached two-car garage encroaching on side lot line setbacks at 22 Newton Street.
22-newton-street-variance.status: The variance application to construct a detached two-car garage at 22 Newton Street was withdrawn without prejudice on June 10, 2026. The withdrawal followed concerns from the Zoning Board of Appeals and Board of Health regarding zero-foot side setbacks and blocked equipment access for septic system maintenance. No further hearings are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 10, 2026, to allow the applicant to withdraw without prejudice so the homeowner can reconsider options.

22-turnpike-road.name: 22 Turnpike Road site plan modification
22-turnpike-road.description: Site plan modification to expand stormwater infiltration, permit existing patios and a shed, and address sports lighting at 22 Turnpike Road.
22-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board approved the major site plan modification for the 22 Turnpike Road golf driving range on October 19, 2026, concluding its public hearing. The approval includes conditions requiring stormwater test pits during construction to verify separation from groundwater and limits exterior lighting to outdoor illumination bylaw standards. The Conservation Commission previously granted a negative determination of applicability in April 2026 for a storage shed on the property.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Oct 19, 2026, to approve the site plan modification with conditions on lighting controls and construction test pits.
Voted 5-0 on Apr 30, 2026, to issue a negative determination of applicability for an equipment storage shed outside the wetland buffer zone.

229-parkerville-road-coc.name: 229 Parkerville Road Certificate of Compliance
229-parkerville-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review and buffer zone encroachment resolution for a fenced garden at 229 Parkerville Road.
229-parkerville-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission reached an agreement with the homeowner of 229 Parkerville Road to resolve a garden encroachment into the 20-foot no-disturb buffer zone. Under the agreement, the existing split-rail fence may remain as the permanent work limit, while trellises extending beyond it must be removed to allow the area to revegetate naturally. Formal action on the Certificate of Compliance remains deferred pending a final site inspection.

positions.detail: Agreed on June 4, 2026, to let the split-rail fence remain in place once gardening trellises beyond the fence are removed.

229-parkerville-road-coc.next: Conservation agent follow-up site visit in fall 2026.

250-turnpike-road.name: 250 Turnpike Road 40B development
250-turnpike-road.description: Comprehensive permit application under Chapter 40B for residential development at 250 Turnpike Road.
250-turnpike-road.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit in May 2026 for a 32-unit rental townhouse development, but vertical construction cannot begin until wastewater and environmental permits are secured. The Conservation Commission's review of the project's Notice of Intent is ongoing and awaiting an environmental peer review report. Although the Board of Health granted a septic pump chamber variance in September 2026, the overall wastewater replacement plan still requires state and conservation approvals.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on May 6, 2026, to approve the comprehensive permit with revised conditions and waivers for the 32-unit project.
Continued the Notice of Intent hearing on Oct 8, 2026, while awaiting a peer review report from Lucas Environmental.
Voted 2-1 on Sep 15, 2026, to grant a foundation setback variance for the project's septic pump chamber subject to a vapor barrier condition.
Sent comments to the ZBA citing unaddressed concerns about property boundary shifts, tree discrepancies, and site plan noncompliance.
Abutters urged the town to downsize the project to 28 units, verify financial waivers, and mandate six-foot privacy fencing and stormwater protections near the Sudbury Reservoir watershed.

26-meadow-lane-coc.name: 26 Meadow Lane Certificate of Compliance
26-meadow-lane-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review for trench drain installation and invasive species monitoring at 26 Meadow Lane under DEP File 290-1087.
26-meadow-lane-coc.status: The matter is fully resolved. The Conservation Commission voted unanimously in March 2026 to issue the Certificate of Compliance for DEP File 290-1087 following confirmation that required invasive species monitoring was completed. No further action is required.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on March 12, 2026, to issue the Certificate of Compliance after confirming receipt of two years of monitoring reports.

27-pine-hill-road-coc.name: 27 Pine Hill Road Certificate of Compliance
27-pine-hill-road-coc.description: Request for a Certificate of Compliance under DEP file 290-1128 for an inground pool within a riverfront area at 27 Pine Hill Road.
27-pine-hill-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission approved a Certificate of Compliance for an in-ground pool at 27 Pine Hill Road on October 8, 2026. The conservation agent reported that all conditions were satisfied, including the installation of a split-rail fence, establishment of native shrubs, and overall site stability. With the certificate issued, the matter is concluded.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Oct 8 to issue the Certificate of Compliance after the agent confirmed compliance with all conditions.

34-turnpike-road-special-permit.name: 34 Turnpike Road special permit
34-turnpike-road-special-permit.description: Special permit review and zoning compliance for unpermitted construction and renovations exceeding approvals at 34 Turnpike Road.
34-turnpike-road-special-permit.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted 1.3 feet of side setback relief to resolve as-built deviations on unpermitted construction, closing the public hearing on June 10, 2026. Approval is conditioned on the applicant removing an unauthorized foundation bump-out encroaching on septic setbacks and obtaining Board of Health certification that the septic capacity supports the dwelling's bedroom count. A formal review and determination from the Board of Health remain pending.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 10, 2026, to approve the side setback relief on the condition that the Board of Health certifies septic capacity.
A representative for the abutter at 32 Turnpike Road opposed the relief, arguing the expansion created an unpermitted four-bedroom house with inadequate septic review.

352-turnpike-road-site-plan.name: 352 Turnpike Road major site plan
352-turnpike-road-site-plan.description: Major site plan approval for Disability Assistance and Vocational Education Inc. at 352 Turnpike Road.
352-turnpike-road-site-plan.status: The Planning Board's review of the major site plan application for an educational and residential facility at 352 Turnpike Road remains open following discussions on Dover Amendment eligibility. Town counsel confirmed the facility qualifies for Dover protections, and the Board of Health confirmed existing septic capacity is sufficient. The applicant agreed to third-party fire suppression review and was asked to identify which exterior lights will stay on overnight for safety.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Feb 23, 2026, to extend its review while awaiting an updated overnight lighting plan and resolving fire suppression conditions.

355-turnpike-road-coc.name: 355 Turnpike Road Certificate of Compliance
355-turnpike-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review, unapproved paving, and stormwater maintenance for a commercial site at 355 Turnpike Road.
355-turnpike-road-coc.status: The request for a Certificate of Compliance for 355 Turnpike Road remains on hold before the Conservation Commission pending site cleanup and documentation. An August inspection revealed unpermitted pavement expansion, uncleaned catch basins showing an oil sheen, and an uncleared stormwater outlet. The commission kept the matter tabled without action on September 17 while awaiting basin maintenance and engineering clarification.

positions.detail: Tabled the Certificate of Compliance request pending catch basin maintenance, site cleanup, and engineering clarification on unpermitted paving.

361-turnpike-road.name: 361 Turnpike Road Valvoline site plan
361-turnpike-road.description: Site plan compliance, as-built review, and occupancy permitting for the Valvoline facility at 361 Turnpike Road.
361-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board voted 4-0 on November 2, 2026, to approve a 90-day temporary certificate of occupancy for the newly constructed Valvoline facility at 361 Turnpike Road. The approval is subject to several outstanding punch-list conditions, including submitting compliant photometric lighting plans, addressing landscaping details, and recording a final as-built plan showing a fire hydrant easement. The applicant must complete these remaining requirements within the 90-day temporary occupancy period.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on November 2, 2026, to grant a 90-day temporary certificate of occupancy subject to punch-list conditions on lighting, landscaping, and final plan recordings.

39-meeting-house-lane-affordable-unit.name: 39 Meeting House Lane right of first refusal
39-meeting-house-lane-affordable-unit.description: Town review of statutory right of first refusal for the resale of an affordable homeownership condominium unit at 39 Meeting House Lane.
39-meeting-house-lane-affordable-unit.status: The town has declined to exercise its right of first refusal to purchase the deed-restricted affordable condominium at 39 Meeting House Lane, clearing the way for a private resale. Both the Affordable Housing Trust Fund and the Select Board determined municipal purchase was unnecessary because deed restrictions keep the home affordable to income-qualified buyers. The property will be offered through an upcoming lottery managed with CHAPA, with town staff reviewing potential local and municipal employee preferences.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0-1 on March 3 to decline interest and waive the town's right of first refusal, allowing the unit to proceed to lottery.
Declined interest in purchasing the property, citing existing deed restrictions that ensure continued affordability.

40-42-central-street.name: 40-42 Central Street site plan compliance
40-42-central-street.description: Resolution of site plan discrepancies, parking configurations, and occupancy permitting for 40-42 Central Street.
40-42-central-street.status: The local zoning appeal regarding occupancy permitting at 40-42 Central Street was withdrawn without prejudice on October 21, 2026, after the state Building Code Appeals Board directed the town to issue a full certificate of occupancy. Although the certificate of occupancy has been issued, site plan compliance items—including accessible parking paving and inspection—remain pending before the town and the Planning Board, which previously recommended revoking the property's temporary certificate of occupancy. No further hearings are currently scheduled before the Zoning Board of Appeals.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Oct 21 to grant the applicant's withdrawal without prejudice after the state-ordered certificate of occupancy rendered the local appeal moot.
Previously voted 4-1 to recommend revoking the property's temporary certificate of occupancy and cited unresolved site plan compliance and threatened litigation.
Requested and was granted withdrawal of its zoning appeal without prejudice after securing a full certificate of occupancy through the state Building Code Appeals Board.

55-plus-housing-bylaw.name: 55-plus housing zoning bylaw amendment
55-plus-housing-bylaw.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendment to eliminate caps on age-restricted 55-plus developments and clarify affordability requirements.
55-plus-housing-bylaw.status: The Affordable Housing Trust reached consensus on Oct 28, 2026, to advance a revised zoning amendment that removes Southborough's 7 percent townwide cap on age-restricted senior housing while establishing a two-acre minimum lot size, an eight-unit-per-acre density limit, and a 12.5 percent affordability mandate. The initiative revives an effort paused in February 2026, when the Planning Board voted unanimously to withdraw an earlier draft from the Annual Town Meeting warrant to examine community concerns over density and housing diversity. Trust members are still discussing enforcement details and fractional payment alternatives for required affordable units. The Trust plans to present the draft to the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, and Select Board in late November or early December 2026 ahead of a future Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Reached consensus on Oct 28, 2026, to endorse Option 2, which eliminates the 7 percent elderly housing cap and requires 12.5 percent affordable units.
Voted 5-0 in February 2026 to withdraw an earlier draft from the warrant for further study following resident concerns regarding density and townwide housing diversity.

55-plus-housing-bylaw.next: Presentations of the draft bylaw to the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, and Select Board in late November or early December 2026.

6-lynbrook-road-enforcement-order.name: 6 Lynbrook Road enforcement order release
6-lynbrook-road-enforcement-order.description: Release of a 2013 Conservation Commission enforcement order regarding unpermitted work on adjacent DCR aqueduct land at 6 Lynbrook Road.
6-lynbrook-road-enforcement-order.status: The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 on October 8 to lift a 2013 enforcement order against 6 Lynbrook Road. The outstanding order, uncovered during a title search for an ongoing home sale, concerned an unpermitted retaining wall and mowing on adjacent state aqueduct land. Following confirmation from the Department of Conservation and Recreation and a site inspection verifying the encroachments were removed, the matter is resolved and the deed cleared.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Oct 8 to lift the enforcement order after verifying the retaining wall was removed and state land restored.

6-walker-street-variance.name: 6 Walker Street garage setback variance
6-walker-street-variance.description: Petition to modify a 1965 variance condition and grant a 6.5-foot side setback variance to construct a garage addition at 6 Walker Street.
6-walker-street-variance.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously approved the application on July 15, 2026, modifying a 1965 variance condition to grant a 6.5-foot side setback variance for a garage addition at 6 Walker Street. Relief was granted based on site constraints and septic placement that made alternative locations impractical. The public hearing is closed, and no further board action is required.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on July 15, 2026, to grant the variance relief citing practical difficulties with lot shape and septic location.
Abutters submitted letters of support for the variance, and no opposition was voiced.

65c-school-street-coc.name: 65C School Street Certificate of Compliance
65c-school-street-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review following unpermitted brush clearing and wetland buffer zone remediation at 65C School Street.
65c-school-street-coc.status: The Conservation Commission approved a Certificate of Compliance for 65C School Street on July 29, 2026. The approval followed remediation by the homeowner, who restored the 20-foot wetland buffer zone and submitted updated as-built plans after unpermitted brush clearing earlier in the year. The matter is resolved with no further town actions scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on July 29, 2026, to issue the Certificate of Compliance after confirming the buffer zone had been properly restored.

66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.name: 66 Breakneck Hill Road septic variance
66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.description: Septic system upgrade and wetland setback variance to support converting a commercial building to residential use at 66 Breakneck Hill Road.
66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved a septic variance on October 13 to support converting a commercial building at 66 Breakneck Hill Road into a four-bedroom single-family home. The variance allows an 85-foot wetland setback near drinking water tributaries instead of the standard 100 feet, improving upon the existing system's 79-foot setback. The project remains contingent on approval from the Conservation Commission and final sign-off from the health agent.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Oct 13 to approve the variance, noting the upgraded nitrogen-reducing system improves upon existing conditions near the wetland.

7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.name: 7 Turnpike Road bodywork compliance
7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.description: Town bodywork permitting compliance and cease-and-desist enforcement for an unlicensed massage business operating at 7 Turnpike Road.
7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.status: The Board of Health unanimously denied the establishment license application for Jojo Bodywork following months of enforcement actions and operation during a cease-and-desist order. Health department staff and town counsel were authorized to draft and execute a formal written decision of the denial. No further hearings or proceedings are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on Aug 11 to deny the license application, citing missing practitioner credentials, unapproved aliases, and operation during an active cease-and-desist order.

8-partridge-hill-road-variance.name: 8 Partridge Hill Road septic variance
8-partridge-hill-road-variance.description: Septic repair variance regarding groundwater separation and setback to the Sudbury Reservoir at 8 Partridge Hill Road.
8-partridge-hill-road-variance.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved the requested variances on August 11, 2026, allowing the replacement of a failed 1975 septic system at 8 Partridge Hill Road. The approval permits a reduced groundwater separation of 2.5 feet and a setback of approximately 230 feet from the Sudbury Reservoir. The Department of Conservation and Recreation raised no objections to the direct-replacement plan, and no further municipal reviews are scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on Aug 11 to grant variances reducing groundwater separation to 2.5 feet and reservoir setback to approximately 230 feet.

911-field-bond-and-fees.name: 911 Field bond repayment and fees
911-field-bond-and-fees.description: Debt service repayment schedule and revolving fund athletic field user fees for the 911 Field turf complex.
911-field-bond-and-fees.status: The Recreation Commission is reviewing the debt repayment schedule and athletic field rental rates for the 911 Field turf complex, as revolving fund revenues have lagged behind pre-COVID projections. Commissioners are considering a $5 to $10 per hour fee increase for sports leagues to help sustain annual bond paybacks of $30,000 to $45,000 to the General Fund through FY35. A decision remains pending while staff finalize updated revenue and debt service models.

positions.detail: Weighing modest hourly field fee increases and an adjusted bond repayment schedule after deferring a vote for refined financial modeling.

911-field-marlborough-trail-connector.name: 911 Field to Marlborough trail connector
911-field-marlborough-trail-connector.description: Exploration and mapping of a potential pedestrian trail link between Southborough's 911 Field and Marlborough trail network.
911-field-marlborough-trail-connector.status: The proposed trail connection between Southborough's 9/11 Field and the Marlborough trail network is currently under early exploration. A Trails Committee member is scouting and mapping the informal route along the waterway and checking whether the Department of Conservation and Recreation will permit formal trail establishment. The committee is awaiting those findings before deciding whether to move forward.

positions.detail: Supports exploring the link and tasked a member with scouting the route and consulting DCR on land permissions.

accessory-dwelling-units-zoning.name: Accessory Dwelling Units zoning amendment
accessory-dwelling-units-zoning.description: Zoning bylaw amendments aligning local regulations with state Affordable Homes Act requirements for accessory dwelling units.
accessory-dwelling-units-zoning.status: Town Meeting approved Article 29 in April 2026, amending the zoning bylaw to allow accessory dwelling units up to 1,200 square feet by right, exceeding the state baseline of 900 square feet. The measure passed with the backing of the Select Board, Planning Board, and Zoning Board of Appeals, but was opposed by the Advisory Committee over concerns about density, septic limitations, and school impacts. All accessory units remain subject to Title 5 septic regulations, height caps, setback limits, and parking requirements.

positions.detail: Sponsored the amendment to expand by-right ADUs up to 1,200 square feet, citing equity for smaller homes and the square footage needed for accessible units.
Voted 5-0 on March 10, 2026, to support the ADU zoning amendment on the Annual Town Meeting warrant.
Supported the amendment in a 4-0-1 vote after holding public hearings to align the local bylaw with state housing regulations.
Voted 2-5 on April 6, 2026, to recommend disapproval, citing concerns about density, school impacts, and allowing large secondary dwellings without special permit oversight.

Residents at Town Meeting were divided, with one speaker arguing 1,200 square feet threatens single-family neighborhood character and another supporting it as an equitable option for housing relatives.

affordable-housing-trust-zoning-cleanup.name: Affordable Housing Trust code reference cleanup
affordable-housing-trust-zoning-cleanup.description: Town Meeting warrant article updating the zoning code to replace references to SHOPC with the Southborough Affordable Housing Trust.
affordable-housing-trust-zoning-cleanup.status: The zoning code cleanup has been approved. Town Meeting voted by a two-thirds majority on April 11, 2026, to pass Article 30, updating the town code to replace references to the dissolved Southborough Housing Opportunity Partnership Committee with the Southborough Affordable Housing Trust. With the vote concluded, no further action is pending.

positions.detail: Approved Article 30 by a two-thirds vote on April 11, 2026.
Sponsored and presented the corrective zoning amendment at Town Meeting following public hearings in early 2026.

algonquin-cell-phone-policy.name: Algonquin high school cell phone policy
algonquin-cell-phone-policy.description: Cell phone restrictions and evaluation of geofencing software at Algonquin Regional High School.
algonquin-cell-phone-policy.status: The planned rollout of the Doorman geofencing mobile app at Algonquin Regional High School is on indefinite hold due to technical delays and concerns regarding student privacy and surveillance. In the interim, the high school continues to require that cell phones be kept off and away in classroom canvas caddies. School administration is seeking additional student and community feedback through a steering committee while monitoring stalled state legislation on school cell phone bans.

positions.detail: Speakers, including parents and an Algonquin student, opposed the Doorman app and supported halting its rollout, citing data privacy, cybersecurity risks, and school committee oversight.

appointed-town-clerk.name: Appointed town clerk transition
appointed-town-clerk.description: Proposal to transition the town clerk from an elected office to an appointed position, including interim clerk appointments.
appointed-town-clerk.status: A home rule petition to convert the town clerk from an elected office to an appointed position is pending at the state legislature after the Select Board voted on October 23, 2026, to formally urge state Representative Kate Donaghue to advance the bill. Amy Berry currently serves as interim town clerk under an appointment running through May 11, 2027, filling the vacancy left by retired clerk Jim Hegarty. Town Meeting previously approved the transition, which voters could finalize either through special state legislation or an upcoming town election ballot question.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on October 23, 2026, to send a letter urging the state legislature to advance the special act making the position appointed.
Voted 6-0 on September 16, 2026, to recommend making the clerk appointed, citing the role's technical complexity and the need for a wider hiring pool.
Residents speaking at Town Meeting split between emphasizing the technical expertise required for modern elections and insisting voters should continue choosing the clerk at the ballot box.

appointed-town-clerk.next: Annual Town Election ballot question on May 11, 2027.

atwood-property-remediation.name: Atwood property environmental remediation
atwood-property-remediation.description: Capital borrowing and environmental site remediation planning for the municipal Atwood property.
atwood-property-remediation.status: Remediation of lead-contaminated soil at the former Atwood Road water tank site is slated for a borrowing vote under Article 9 at the fall Special Town Meeting, following a spring decision to postpone the estimated $800,000 to $850,000 appropriation. Officials previously canceled active bids to allow time for temporary site stabilization and public discussion on future site uses. Key resident questions focus on how contractors will verify lead removal and whether remediation will be separated on the warrant from potential affordable housing proposals.

positions.detail: Agreed to cancel earlier bids and prepare Article 9 for fall Town Meeting action after reviewing an $800,000 to $850,000 soil removal plan.
Voted 5-0 to recommend postponing the appropriation to the fall special town meeting to give residents time to consider future site uses.
Atwood Road residents asked how lead removal would be verified during excavation and whether cleanup would remain distinct from future housing plans.

atwood-property-remediation.next: Select Board discussion on Atwood tank soil remediation options later in November 2026.

board-of-health-body-art-regulations.name: Board of Health body art regulations
board-of-health-body-art-regulations.description: Revisions to municipal body art regulations regarding practitioner training, apprenticeships, and prohibited activities.
board-of-health-body-art-regulations.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved revisions to the town's body art regulations in June 2026. The updated rules align local standards with state models, reinstate training and apprenticeship requirements for practitioners, and add vaping to the list of activities prohibited in procedure areas. The matter is concluded with no further action pending.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on June 9, 2026, to adopt the updated regulations, including an amendment prohibiting vaping in procedure areas.

breakneck-hill-restoration.name: Breakneck Hill Conservation Land restoration
breakneck-hill-restoration.description: Planning and invasive species management for a comprehensive five-zone ecological restoration at Breakneck Hill Conservation Land.
breakneck-hill-restoration.status: The Stewardship Committee is preparing a formal scope of work with the town planner to solicit bids for a five-zone ecological restoration of Breakneck Hill Conservation Land. The project addresses invasive species management, soil compaction from heavy equipment, site grading, botanical surveys, and native replanting, utilizing $47,000 recovered from remediation contractors. A committee liaison was appointed in August to coordinate with the invasive management contractor as planning proceeds.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Aug 4 to appoint a liaison to the invasive plant management contractor while developing a comprehensive restoration scope with the town planner.

brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.name: Brox asphalt plant complaints
brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.description: Intermunicipal response and MassDEP oversight regarding resident noise and odor complaints concerning the Brox Industries asphalt plant in Marlborough.
brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.status: Southborough continues to monitor resident noise and odor complaints concerning the Brox Industries asphalt plant in Marlborough, though Town Counsel has advised that the town has no legal jurisdiction over the out-of-town facility. MassDEP confirmed the facility operates within federal permit limits, but residents continue to report persistent odors despite Brox's installation of a closed-loop burner exhaust mitigation system. Health department staff are tracking real-time resident odor logs and coordinating with state regulators and Marlborough officials.

positions.detail: Tracking resident reports and coordinating with MassDEP while noting that Southborough lacks enforcement authority over the Marlborough plant.
Neighbors reported chemical and burnt-rubber odors and morning noise, and requested that Southborough and Marlborough jointly fund an independent air quality consultant.

cannabis-delivery-opt-out.name: Cannabis delivery opt-out waiver
cannabis-delivery-opt-out.description: Deliberation on whether Southborough should request a state waiver from the Cannabis Control Commission to prohibit adult-use cannabis home delivery.
cannabis-delivery-opt-out.status: Adult-use cannabis home delivery is permitted in Southborough after the Select Board voted against applying for a state opt-out waiver. The Board of Health reviewed the issue earlier without taking a formal stance, weighing youth access concerns against parity with alcohol delivery. With the opt-out rejected, licensed couriers may deliver to adult residents aged 21 and older, and no further action is scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 1-4 on Aug 11 against applying for a two-year state opt-out waiver, allowing licensed home delivery to proceed.
Declined to take a formal stance on July 7, sending the Select Board a memo outlining divided views on youth health risks versus adult access.
A resident favored opting out, questioning whether doorstep ID checks would be enforced and doubting any public benefit.

cemetery-expansion.name: Town cemetery expansion planning
cemetery-expansion.description: Site evaluation and capacity planning to identify and acquire land for a new municipal cemetery.
cemetery-expansion.status: Town cemetery expansion planning is under review as the ad hoc Cemetery Expansion Committee evaluates 58 candidate parcels of five or more acres for a new municipal cemetery. With Rural Cemetery sold out and Middle Road Cemetery projected to reach capacity around 2035 or 2036, the committee is developing a screening matrix to narrow down potential sites. The Select Board backs the planning effort and voted in September to reduce the committee's size to maintain quorums. The committee expects to present final site recommendations before June.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to reduce the expansion committee's membership to three to achieve quorums and maintain progress on capacity planning.
Is vetting 58 candidate properties of five or more acres to recommend a site before Middle Road Cemetery exhausts its remaining 458 plots.

classification-and-compensation-study.name: Municipal classification and compensation study
classification-and-compensation-study.description: A comprehensive classification and compensation study evaluating 48 non-union municipal employee positions.
classification-and-compensation-study.status: The draft classification and compensation study is under review after the Personnel Board voted to adopt a 12-grade salary schedule aligned to the 60th percentile of regional peer communities. Multiple department heads and staff members have pushed back against proposed job gradings and titles, particularly objecting to grouping diverse responsibilities under a broad Business Administrator classification. A three-member review panel will assess employee appeals submitted by late November before final recommendations are prepared for an Annual Town Meeting warrant article targeting implementation in July 2027.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on October 30, 2026 to adopt the 60th percentile benchmark and set an employee appeals process for the proposed 12-grade plan.
Department heads and staff expressed dissatisfaction with proposed job grades, questioned discrepancies across departments, and urged the town to protect longevity and credentials.

classification-and-compensation-study.next: Employee reconsideration appeal deadline on November 24, 2026.

classroom-interactive-touch-displays.name: Classroom interactive touch displays
classroom-interactive-touch-displays.description: A $365,000 capital request for the Annual Town Meeting warrant to install Newline interactive touch displays across K-8 classrooms.
classroom-interactive-touch-displays.status: The installation of interactive touch displays across all Southborough K-8 classrooms is now complete. The $365,000 capital project, backed by town boards ahead of the 2026 Annual Town Meeting, replaced 10- to 11-year-old projectors with 75- to 96-inch interactive panels across all district schools. With hardware installation finished, district staff are now proceeding with teacher training.

positions.detail: Requested the $365,000 capital appropriation to replace failing classroom projectors with interactive panels across K-8 schools.
Voted unanimously on Mar 17 to support the capital borrowing article on the Annual Town Meeting warrant.
Voted 3-0 on Mar 18 to support the school capital bonding article.
Voted 3-2 on Mar 16 to recommend the $365,000 FY27 capital bond for school technology.

commercial-drone-delivery-oversight.name: Commercial drone delivery oversight
commercial-drone-delivery-oversight.description: Town review and regional advocacy concerning federal permitting and community impacts of Amazon commercial drone deliveries.
commercial-drone-delivery-oversight.status: The Select Board voted unanimously on October 23, 2026, to join neighboring communities in signing a joint letter to the Federal Aviation Administration and Amazon requesting more study, public meetings, and data before commercial drone deliveries launch. Members cited concerns regarding potential noise, emergency service call volume surges, and environmental trade-offs compared to delivery vans. The letter will be executed by either the board chair or the town administrator.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Oct 23 to sign a joint letter urging the FAA and Amazon to conduct further study and public meetings before launching drone deliveries.

community-preservation-appropriations.name: Community Preservation statutory appropriations
community-preservation-appropriations.description: Annual Town Meeting appropriations for Community Preservation Act statutory reserves, debt service, and administrative expenses.
community-preservation-appropriations.status: The Community Preservation Committee has moved on to the FY27 funding cycle, conducting preliminary technical reviews of new project applications. During the 2026 Annual Town Meeting preparations, the Select Board reversed an earlier unanimous opposition vote to endorse Article 22, which funded statutory reserves and $29,000 in administrative expenses. Board discussions also highlighted concerns regarding 18 older CPA projects totaling roughly $79,000 that remain open primarily because required statutory signs have not yet been installed.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0-1 on March 10, 2026, to recommend Article 22, reversing a prior 5-0 vote to oppose the $29,000 administrative appropriation.
Sponsored Article 22 to allocate statutory reserves and administrative funds, noting that legacy projects remain open because statutory signage is still pending.
Residents suggested standardizing CPA signage with QR codes to cut costs and reduce clutter, and urged clear milestones to avoid multi-year project delays.

conservation-land-use-regulations.name: Conservation land use regulations
conservation-land-use-regulations.description: Adoption and amendment of town code regulations governing public use and activities on town-owned conservation land.
conservation-land-use-regulations.status: The Conservation Commission adopted town-wide conservation land use regulations under Section 43-2 of the Southborough Town Code on April 30, 2026. The new rules give the commission formal enforcement authority over violations and encroachments, such as unauthorized mowing on town-owned open space. While the regulations are now in effect, the commission noted that future amendments may be considered at later meetings to address matters like exterior light trespass from abutting parcels.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on April 30, 2026, to adopt the land use regulations under Town Code Section 43-2 to establish enforcement authority over conservation parcels.
Provided recommended revisions to the draft rules, which the Conservation Commission incorporated prior to formal adoption.

constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.name: Constitution Drive drainage and street acceptance
constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.description: Sinkhole repair at 11 Constitution Drive and resolution of unrecorded municipal street and drainage easements.
constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.status: The Select Board authorized DPW to perform an estimated $5,000 one-time sinkhole repair at 11 Constitution Drive, conditioned on a signed right-of-entry and hold-harmless agreement from the homeowner. The recurring sinkhole sits over a 17.5-foot-deep town storm drainage pipe on a street where Town Meeting approved acceptance in the past, but final deeds were never recorded. Town staff and town counsel are currently investigating options to resolve the unrecorded street and drainage easements.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Sep 2 to authorize DPW's driveway repair under a hold-harmless agreement and directed staff to explore legal steps to rectify unrecorded easements.

costco-special-act-liquor-license.name: Costco special act liquor license
costco-special-act-liquor-license.description: Proposed special state legislation authorizing an additional off-premises liquor license in Southborough for Costco.
costco-special-act-liquor-license.status: The governor signed special legislation granting Southborough the authority to issue an additional off-premises alcohol license for Costco. Under the enacted law, the town has until October 4, 2028, to issue the license before the authorization expires. The Select Board now has authority to formally grant the license.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 in March 2026 to back the Town Meeting petition and submitted testimony in favor before the bill was signed into law.

cpa-affordable-housing-trust-transfer.name: CPA transfer to Affordable Housing Trust
cpa-affordable-housing-trust-transfer.description: Annual transfer of Community Preservation Act funds to support the Southborough Affordable Housing Trust.
cpa-affordable-housing-trust-transfer.status: Following Town Meeting's approval of a $61,000 transfer in April 2026, the Affordable Housing Trust is pursuing its next Community Preservation Act funding allocation. The application is currently under review by the Community Preservation Committee, which raised minor questions regarding survey data. Trust staff and members are preparing the updated data while coordinating with MassHousing Partnership on technical assistance and project financing.

positions.detail: Submitted a CPA funding application and is gathering updated survey data to answer technical review questions.
Voted by majority on April 11, 2026, to approve Article 25 transferring $61,000 to the trust.

cpa-project-signage-program.name: CPA project signage program
cpa-project-signage-program.description: Development of townwide signage and markers for past and ongoing Community Preservation Act-funded projects.
cpa-project-signage-program.status: The Community Preservation Committee is developing standardized signage to recognize CPA contributions across past and ongoing project sites in town. The committee has finalized plaque language for the Town House and clarified specific sizing and placement guidelines for sites including Harold E. Fay Memorial Park, Mooney Field, and the Richardson Tennis Courts. Members also agreed not to add duplicate signage at the South Union School as they prepare to order signs.

positions.detail: Is advancing standardized signage templates and finalizing wording and location plans across CPA-funded municipal properties.

culvert-infrastructure-replacements.name: Culvert infrastructure replacements
culvert-infrastructure-replacements.description: Town-wide culvert replacements funded through a state grant to replace previously authorized borrowing.
culvert-infrastructure-replacements.status: Southborough is proceeding with town-wide culvert replacements after receiving nearly $3.9 million from the Massachusetts Community Culvert Grant Program, which allows the town to avoid taking on new debt. To support culvert work and flood prevention on Willow Street, the Select Board accepted three permanent private drainage easements in August 2026 following Town Meeting authorization in April. The town expects to eventually rescind its previously approved $3.9 million borrowing authorization.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on August 11, 2026, to accept three drainage easements on Willow Street to advance the culvert replacement project.
Approved Article 27 by a two-thirds majority on April 11, 2026, authorizing the Select Board to acquire the Willow Street drainage easements.
Voted 6-0 on March 25, 2026, to recommend approval of Article 27 authorizing the Willow Street easements.

decertified-library-borrowing-policy.name: Decertified library borrowing policy
decertified-library-borrowing-policy.description: Library Board of Trustees policy restricting physical borrowing privileges for patrons from municipalities with decertified public libraries.
decertified-library-borrowing-policy.status: The Library Board of Trustees approved a policy restricting physical borrowing privileges for patrons residing in municipalities with decertified public libraries. Under the policy, affected patrons retain building access, computer access, and event attendance, while CW MARS will block physical item checkouts. Trustees noted the policy can be revisited if neighboring towns face decertification in future budget cycles.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on Oct 5 to adopt the CW MARS model policy restricting physical borrowing for patrons from decertified communities.

downtown-wayfinding-plan.name: Downtown Southborough Wayfinding Plan
downtown-wayfinding-plan.description: A state grant-funded planning study to design and install directional, gateway, and informational signage across downtown Southborough.
downtown-wayfinding-plan.status: The draft wayfinding plan to install gateway, directional, and pedestrian signage across downtown Southborough remains under review by town officials. While reviewing early concepts, the Select Board and Historical Commission cautioned against visual clutter and suburban aesthetics, urging consultants to incorporate omitted historic destinations such as the Community House, Rural Cemetery, and Burnett Mansion. Town administration plans to seek a Phase 2 state grant to fund detailed fabrication specifications and eventual sign installation.

positions.detail: Cautions against sign clutter and modern suburban designs, while insisting that key historic landmarks must be integrated into the wayfinding system.
Reviewed the draft plan in June 2026, noting community preference for simpler designs and requesting the addition of historic locations before pursuing fabrication grants.

facilities-van-replacement.name: Facilities Department replacement van
facilities-van-replacement.description: Emergency capital funding and potential Reserve Fund transfer to replace an out-of-service Facilities Department van.
facilities-van-replacement.status: The emergency replacement of the condemned 2018 Facilities Department utility van has been fully funded. Following agreement with the Select Board to remove the purchase from the Annual Town Meeting warrant, the Advisory Committee voted unanimously in March 2026 to approve a $75,000 Reserve Fund transfer. The transfer enabled the town to order the replacement immediately and end ongoing vehicle rental fees.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on March 16, 2026, to approve a $75,000 Reserve Fund transfer so the department could purchase a replacement van immediately.
Supported funding the estimated $70,000 to $71,000 replacement through the Reserve Fund rather than adding it to the Town Meeting warrant.
Voted 3-0 on March 9, 2026, to add the emergency $75,000 request to the capital plan on the condition that it would not displace other recommended items.

fay-school-25-middle-road.name: Fay School 25 Middle Road addition
fay-school-25-middle-road.description: Review of as-built plans, construction discrepancies, and landscape mitigation for an addition at Fay School's 25 Middle Road campus.
fay-school-25-middle-road.status: The Planning Board voted 4-0 on November 2, 2026, to approve the final landscape mitigation plan and as-built engineering plans for Fay School's building addition at 25 Middle Road. The board also recommended that the building commissioner issue a certificate of occupancy before the school's temporary permit expires on November 19. Peer review engineers confirmed drainage and stormwater compliance, noting only that high flow velocities in an adjusted drainage pipe section will require ongoing maintenance checks. The final decision on the occupancy permit now rests with the building commissioner.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on November 2, 2026, to approve the Version 3 landscape mitigation plan, accept as-builts, and recommend issuance of an occupancy permit.

fay-school-athletic-fields.name: Fay School athletic fields redevelopment
fay-school-athletic-fields.description: Notice of Intent and redevelopment to convert grass soccer fields to artificial turf and relocate a baseball field at Fay School's 0 Marlboro Junction property.
fay-school-athletic-fields.status: The Notice of Intent and stormwater management permit application to convert grass fields to artificial turf and relocate a baseball field at Fay School's 0 Marlborough Junction property remains under review. The Conservation Commission has not yet deliberated on the merits of work within the wetland buffer zone and riverfront area, having granted repeated continuance requests from the applicant without substantive presentation. A substantive public hearing before the commission will be the next step once rescheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on Oct 8 to continue the public hearing at the applicant's request without substantive discussion.

fayville-memorial-park-improvements.name: Fayville Memorial Park improvements
fayville-memorial-park-improvements.description: Planning, community outreach, and design improvements for Fayville Memorial Park, including splash pad features and parking capacity.
fayville-memorial-park-improvements.status: The Fayville Memorial Park improvement project is moving toward the March 2027 Annual Town Meeting after the town was awarded a state Land and Water Conservation Fund grant of up to $632,000 covering half of projected costs. The Recreation Commission plans to seek matching Community Preservation Act funding for the splash pad, dog park, and walking trail upgrades after withdrawing an earlier application to resolve site details. Outstanding questions involve legal considerations under Article 97 and finalizing a parking configuration along Central Street that avoids encroaching on park green space. The Recreation Commission plans to meet with the Select Board in December 2026 to finalize parking plans and legal approvals.

positions.detail: Champions the renovation and is finalizing Central Street parking plans after securing a state grant covering half the estimated project costs.
Received project updates but withheld action pending further engineering plans and legal review of Article 97 park protections and roadway parking designs.
Residents raised concerns about sightlines and speeding traffic with proposed Central Street parking, as well as oversight, operational rules, and fee policies for the planned dog park.

fayville-memorial-park-improvements.next: Select Board review of Fayville Park parking layout and approvals in December 2026.

flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.name: Flagg Road and Route 9 hydrant relocation
flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.description: Relocation of a frequently struck fire hydrant and removal of scenic road stone wall at Flagg Road and 361 Turnpike Road.
flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.status: The Planning Board approved a request to remove approximately 10 feet of stone wall along scenic Flagg Road at 361 Turnpike Road. The removal enables the Department of Public Works to relocate a frequently struck fire hydrant roughly 10 feet back into an acquired utility easement. Approval was conditioned on keeping the removed stones on site or reusing them for local wall restoration.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on May 11, 2026, to approve the scenic road stone wall removal with conditions that the stones remain on Flagg Road.
Requested the wall removal to move the fire hydrant out of traffic following repeated vehicle strikes; the request was granted.

fy27-operating-budget.name: FY27 operating budget
fy27-operating-budget.description: Annual municipal operating budget, revenue cap balancing, and omnibus warrant article for fiscal year 2027.
fy27-operating-budget.status: The $71,077,130 FY27 operating budget was approved at the April 2026 Annual Town Meeting following debate over police staffing, employee benefit plans, and committee funding. In November 2026, the Select Board finalized implementation by voting 4-1 to maintain a single tax rate of $14.54 per thousand, resulting in an estimated 5.01 percent increase on the average single-family tax bill, while voting 5-0 against residential and commercial exemptions. The board also signaled interest in exploring future legislation for senior means-tested property tax relief.

positions.detail: Voted on April 11, 2026, to approve the $71,077,130 operating budget under Article 6, including separate votes affirming funding for police, employee benefits, and the Economic Development Committee.
Voted 3-2 to recommend the operating budget in March citing tax impact and headcount concerns, then voted 4-1 in November to adopt a single unified tax rate.
Voted 5-0 on March 16 to recommend the town budget, highlighting health insurance cost-saving models and capital adjustments.

At Town Meeting, residents questioned spending on an inactive Economic Development Committee and rising benefit costs, while others voiced support for police traffic enforcement and EDC regional membership dues.

fy27-regional-school-operating-budget.name: FY27 regional school operating budget
fy27-regional-school-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, reserve transfers, and capital assessments for the Northborough-Southborough Regional School District for fiscal year 2027.
fy27-regional-school-operating-budget.status: The Regional School Committee unanimously approved a revised $31,521,177 FY27 operating budget on October 29, 2026, incorporating an additional $104,890 in state Chapter 70 aid for special education transportation. The update, paired with finalized athletic complex debt figures, slightly reduced Southborough's assessment to $10,731,901. Both member towns have a statutory 45-day window to respond to the revised assessment notices.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Oct 29 to adopt the revised $31,521,177 budget and lower town assessments following an increase in Chapter 70 aid.

fy27-road-paving-contracts.name: FY27 road paving and sidewalk contracts
fy27-road-paving-contracts.description: Procurement and contract awards for fiscal year 2027 DPW road paving and sidewalk maintenance.
fy27-road-paving-contracts.status: The Select Board unanimously approved the fiscal year 2027 contracts for road paving and sidewalk maintenance on September 15, 2026. The awarded contract covers six roads, including interim paving on Cordaville and Cranberry roads ahead of long-term state Transportation Improvement Program projects. Bid pricing came in approximately $400,000 below engineering estimates, and no further municipal approvals are required.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to approve the FY27 paving and sidewalk contract awards, noting bids came in well below estimates.

fy27-school-operating-budget.name: FY27 school operating budget
fy27-school-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, class size staffing, and reserve funding for the Southborough K-8 public schools for fiscal year 2027.
fy27-school-operating-budget.status: The FY27 school operating budget is currently in active execution, with the district maintaining an available balance of $332,720 (1.27% of the budget) as of October 31, 2026. The budget absorbed two additional elementary teachers hired over the summer to maintain class sizes, with internal transfers covering localized deficits in transportation, utilities, and curriculum salaries. Additionally, the School Committee has requested that the Select Board place an unbudgeted $105,485 in state Chapter 70 aid into the town's empty Special Education Stabilization Fund.

positions.detail: Endorsed the 3.99% operating budget in May and voted unanimously on Nov 9 to accept the October expenditure report, approve overexpended function codes, and accept $747,857 in state and federal grants.

fy27-water-enterprise-budget.name: FY27 Water Enterprise budget and capital
fy27-water-enterprise-budget.description: Annual operating budget, non-borrowing capital improvements, and loan authorizations for the Water Enterprise Fund.
fy27-water-enterprise-budget.status: The FY27 Water Enterprise budget of $3,522,752 was approved by Town Meeting in April 2026, funded primarily through water rates and retained earnings. Ahead of Town Meeting, the Select Board unanimously approved a 12.6 percent base charge increase and a 9.0 percent volumetric rate hike to support capital projects and strengthen reserves. Capital items and loan authorizations for main looping also received board endorsements, and no further town action is currently pending.

positions.detail: Approved Article 7 on April 11, 2026, by a two-thirds vote to authorize the $3,522,752 FY27 Water Enterprise budget.
Voted unanimously in February 2026 to increase water rates, and voted in March to recommend Article 7 (4-1), Article 10 (5-0), and Article 11 (4-1).
Voted 3-0 on March 18, 2026, to endorse Article 10 capital items funded through the water enterprise fund.

fy28-capital-budget.name: FY28 capital budget
fy28-capital-budget.description: Planning, departmental request review, and debt financing prioritization for the fiscal year 2028 capital improvement plan.
fy28-capital-budget.status: The FY28 capital improvement plan is under active review as boards evaluate multi-million-dollar requests across municipal and school operations. Submitted priorities include $710,000 for school building repairs and safety fencing, public works plow trucks, state-mandated water tank rehabilitation, and a potential $1.82 million smart water meter conversion. The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee is compiling departmental presentations and maintenance data before delivering its recommendations to the Select Board in early December.

positions.detail: Currently evaluating departmental proposals from public works, water, police, and schools ahead of drafting recommendations in December.
Advanced a $710,000 FY28 capital plan covering school safety fencing, stairs, and sink replacements, while maintaining a $45 million placeholder for Neary.
A resident cautioned that annual construction inflation could outpace MSBA reimbursement benefits if school building project decisions are delayed.

fy28-capital-budget.next: Capital Improvement and Planning Committee meeting to review school department capital requests on November 16, 2026.

fy28-operating-budget.name: FY28 operating budget
fy28-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, multi-year deficit forecasting, and consideration of a Proposition 2 1/2 operational override for fiscal year 2028.
fy28-operating-budget.status: Town officials are evaluating two FY28 budget scenarios: Budget A, which preserves level services but faces a projected $1.4 million deficit requiring a Proposition 2 1/2 operational override, and Budget B, which limits funding to FY27 levels and forces departmental staffing and service cuts. Departments have submitted impact memos outlining cutbacks under Budget B, including reduced office hours, eliminated programming, and curtailed staffing. The Select Board is weighing whether to pursue an override and considering a multi-year structure, while the Advisory Committee has favored tighter spending controls and alternative mechanisms to relieve budget pressures. Department budget hearings with major town departments begin November 17.

positions.detail: Reviewing departmental impact memos and weighing whether to pursue a single-year or multi-year Proposition 2 1/2 operating override to bridge a $1.4 million deficit.
Urged caution regarding large multi-year overrides, advocating instead for strict fiscal controls, an executive hiring freeze, and exploring borrowing mechanisms for pension liabilities.
Voted unanimously on October 30 to approve its FY28 Budget A and B requests after recommending a 5% total salary grid adjustment in September.
Voted 3-0 on October 20 to approve its FY28 budget requests and submit an explanatory memo detailing service reductions required under level funding.
Voted 5-0 on October 14 to approve FY28 budget priorities to guide the district's preliminary budget build.
Voted 6-0 on October 5 to approve its FY28 operating budget while balancing state materials spending ratios against projected cuts.
Voted unanimously on October 7 to approve its FY28 operating budget request of $4,250.
Postponed action on its budget memo in September, expressing strong frustration that Budget B guidelines would force a reduction in conservation agent hours.
A resident cautioned the Select Board that calculating cuts to fractional full-time equivalent positions under Budget B affects more staff and services than numbers suggest.

fy28-operating-budget.next: Select Board review meeting on FY28 budget scenarios with K-8 Schools, DPW, Police, and Fire on November 17, 2026.

fy28-regional-school-operating-budget.name: FY28 regional school operating budget
fy28-regional-school-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, health insurance restructuring, and capital improvement planning for the Northborough-Southborough Regional School District for fiscal year 2028.
fy28-regional-school-operating-budget.status: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School District is developing its FY28 operating budget amid tight municipal Proposition 2 1/2 constraints in both member towns. District administrators are preparing level-service, level-funded, and 3% budget cap models while negotiating employee health insurance deductible changes that could yield about $600,000 in regional savings. The district is also planning warrant articles in Southborough and Northborough to establish a Special Education Stabilization Fund ahead of preliminary budget presentations.

positions.body: Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee Operational Budget and Capital Planning Subcommittees
positions.detail: Directed staff to draft level-service, level-funded, and 3% cap scenarios while recommending a five-year communications plan over adding new personnel.
A resident and municipal finance official urged holding earlier joint discussions during the budget cycle to align terminology and budget assumptions.

fy28-regional-school-operating-budget.next: Preliminary FY28 budget presentation to the Regional School Committee on November 18, 2026.

fy28-school-operating-budget.name: FY28 school operating budget
fy28-school-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, cost reduction scenarios, and class staffing for Southborough K-8 public schools for fiscal year 2028.
fy28-school-operating-budget.status: District administrators presented a preliminary FY28 operating budget of $27,514,571, representing a 5.36% increase driven largely by salaries, transportation, and a 41% rise in out-of-district special education tuition. The Southborough School Committee is currently evaluating reduction scenarios to meet town guidance, which include cutting $616,411 to reach a 3% target or cutting $1.4 million and roughly 15 staff positions under level-funding. Officials will discuss the figures with the Select Board before the superintendent submits a refined recommended budget in December.

positions.detail: Reviewing a preliminary 5.36% increase while weighing reduction scenarios required to meet town guidance targets.

fy28-school-operating-budget.next: Joint meeting with the Select Board on November 17, 2026.

glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.name: Glow SoBo holiday lighting
glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.description: Funding and municipal installation of holiday lighting displays and kickoff event for the Tricentennial.
glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.status: Plans for the Glow SoBo holiday lighting display and celebration are moving forward for early December. The Tricentennial Committee authorized a $10,456 contract for commercial exterior lighting of the Town House, library grounds, and nearby trees, and will fund permanent exterior electrical outlets on the library property. The Library Board of Trustees unanimously approved the outdoor lighting and electrical work, while deferring any decision on hosting indoor after-hours activities.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on Aug 12 to approve a $10,456 contract for professional lighting on municipal buildings and grounds.
Voted unanimously on Sep 14 to approve exterior holiday lighting and the installation of permanent outdoor electrical outlets.

history-makers-recognition-program.name: Tricentennial History Makers recognition program
history-makers-recognition-program.description: Tricentennial initiative honoring notable historical and contemporary Southborough figures.
history-makers-recognition-program.status: The History Makers recognition initiative is currently underway and accepting nominations online to honor notable past and present Southborough residents. Launched in October 2026 by the Tricentennial Committee, the program seeks nominations across civic, scientific, volunteer, and business contributions. Committee members are actively promoting the forms and collecting submissions through town channels.

positions.detail: Launched the online nomination form to recognize residents' civic and community contributions and is actively gathering submissions.

hopkinton-water-connection.name: Hopkinton MWRA water connection
hopkinton-water-connection.description: Proposed intermunicipal agreement to convey MWRA water to the town of Hopkinton through Southborough's distribution system.
